thread:
Eve: heads-up — since we flipped FP8 on the h100 L40S pool this morning, we're seeing p99 latency spikes and a lot of KV cache churn. noticed after 09:20UTC. :alarm:
Ben: confirmed. tail spikes correlate with big bursts of small requests that push batch shape from 1->16 and kernel selector seems to pick a slow PATH. wondering if batching heuristic is overshooting.
Carla: repro attached from staging: 10k short-chat requests in 2m window. KV hit-rate drops from 98% -> 60% during the surge. stack trace shows repeated KV eviction thundering.
perf-bot: perf snapshot (summary):
```
p50: 12ms, p90: 32ms, p95: 45ms, p99: 210ms (prev baseline p99 82ms)
CPU on host: 18% -> 85% during spikes
GPU active kernels: fp8_fused_attention_v2 (fast) then fallback to fp8_generic_matmul_slowpath
KV cache hit: 98% -> 60% on affected hosts
Batch size distribution: 80% <=4, 18% 5-12, 2% >12
```
Alice: that fallback kernel is new: transformer-engine auto mode seems to permit a swap when sequence len or batchshape changes. probably swapping in a compatibility kernel that is scalar/slow.
Ben: hypothesis: batching heuristic tries to maximize throughput by growing batch window; with many short contexts KV cache misses cause rewarm which increases seq_len/batch latency and triggers selector to choose compatibility kernel. the selector's cost model underestimates cold-KV penalty.
Carla: here's the minimal config we used in repro: 
```
model_config:
  quant: FP8
  kernel_selector: heuristic_v4
  transformer_engine: auto
  max_batch_delay_ms: 8
  kv_cache_hot_threshold: 0.7
```
We lowered kv_cache_hot_threshold to 0.5 in a quick test and saw fewer evictions but throughput dipped.
Dave: can we short-circuit kernel selection for these H100 workers and pin the FP8 fused kernel for seq_len<=64 and batch<=8? fallback only for memory-overflow. safer than full revert.
Alice: deploying a canary with selector rule: if device==H100 && quant==FP8 && seq_len<=64 && batch<=8 -> prefer fused_fp8_v2, else normal. rolling to 10 hosts now. CLI patch: 
```
rctl rollout selector-rule add --pool h100-l40s --match "quant==FP8 && seq<=64 && batch<=8" --prefer fused_fp8_v2 --ttl 30m
```
infra-bot: started canary rollout: hosts (h100-012,h100-034,h100-045,h100-078) — patch id r-2026-ctr-88
Carla: early canary metrics: p99 on canary hosts dropped from 210ms -> 165ms, overall p99 across pool dropped ~45ms. KV hit-rate on canary stayed ~95%. but server-side throughput on canary hosts decreased ~3% measured by tokens/sec.
Ben: tradeoff looks acceptable short-term. need to fix selector cost model so it accounts for KV rewarm penalty and batch-growth transient cost. current cost model only uses compute FLOPs and memory footprint, not cache-warmup time.
Eve: agreed. immediate actions: 1) extend telemetry to include KV rewarm latency per-request and expose as tag for kernel selector traces; 2) run micro-benchmarks for fused_fp8_v2 vs fallback across batch shapes with cold/warm KV states; 3) update selector cost model to include empiric rewarm penalty term and re-evaluate; 4) schedule a rollback plan if p99 > 300ms.
Ben: I'll own microbench harness and selector model patch. aiming to post PR with synthetic traces by EOD.
Carla: I'll gather detailed traces and the staging repro artifacts into the incident folder. also adding a small eval: run 1M short requests with intermittent cold cache to measure steady-state oscillation.
Alice: postmortem notes: avoid auto transformer-engine knob for now in h100-l40s for FP8 until selector is improved. we should add an opt-in flag per-deployment to lock kernel families.
Eve: thanks. keep this thread updated with perf diffs. add any surprising traces here — especially cases where batchshape oscillates repeatedly. :mag:
Ben: will do, first logs in 15m.
